newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO SLUMP TO FIRST DEFEAT FOR THREE MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO SLUMP TO FIRST DEFEAT FOR THREE MONTHS.

text.p: Monaco slumped to their first French league defeat for more than three months when they lost 2-0 to Metz on Saturday.
But arch rivals Paris St Germain failed to take full advantage. They were held to a 1-1 home draw by Guingamp.
Monaco, last beaten in the league on November 6 by Marseille, saw their lead over PSG cut to six points.
They fell behind to a Cyril Serredszum header in the 14th minute. Their fate was sealed in injury time when Bruno Rodriguez scored direct from a free kick.
PSG were fortunate to escape with a draw against Guingamp, a team they have never beaten in the league.
Brazilian Rai secured a point when he converted a penalty midway through the second half. Stephane Carnot had given Guingamp the lead direct from a corner in the first half.
"We are very disappointed because we had a fine opportunity to close the gap with Monaco," said PSG striker Cyrille Pouget.
Third-placed Bastia, who have a game in hand, easily disposed of lowly Nancy 2-0. Wilfried Gohel and Anto Drobnjak were their marksmen late in the match.
The clash between Bordeaux and Marseille was disappointingly one-sided, Bordeaux winning 4-0. Marseille's miserable night saw striker Xavier Gravelaine sent off for punching Jean-Pierre Papin.
"He provoked me and I could not help it. It was a silly gesture," Gravelaine said.
Last week Bordeaux qualified for the League Cup final in which they will meet another in-form team, Strasbourg, who won 4-2 away at Lille.
While Strasbourg prosper in fourth place, champions Auxerre continue to struggle. They lost 2-0 at home to Montpellier, Christophe Sanchez scoring twice.
Coach Guy Roux, already without several first-choice players, complained that he had to do without Algerians Moussa Saib and Abdel Tasfaout who were playing in an African Nations' Cup qualifier.
"It's a pity to see players rush to help their national sides at the expense of their clubs," he said.
Montpellier are now unbeaten in 12 league matches.
On Friday, Nantes extended their unbeaten run to 20 matches with a 1-0 win in Rennes.
